This test checks that refactor.inline.variable is rejected for an array
variable that is sliced. Slicing an array implicitly takes its address:
the resulting slice refers to the array's elements, so the array may be
modified through it.

Previously, inlining arr was offered at both uses below:
1. At arr[:], producing [3]int{1, 2, 3}[:], which does not compile
   (cannot slice unaddressable value).
2. At fmt.Println(arr), which would change the printed value, since arr
   was modified through s.

-- go.mod --
module example.com/a
go 1.18

-- a/a.go --
package a

func _() {
	var arr = [3]int{1, 2, 3}
	s := arr[:] //@codeaction("arr", "refactor.inline.variable", err="0 CodeActions of kind refactor.inline.variable")
	s[0] = 9
	println(arr) //@codeaction("arr", "refactor.inline.variable", err="0 CodeActions of kind refactor.inline.variable")
}
